title: Two steps of the validity tester
statement: Let $x$, $p$, and $r$ be Boolean words, let $b,c\in\{0,1\}$, and suppose $x=p\,b\,c\,r$. Starting in the block state at position $|p|$ with empty output, after two steps the tester is still in its block state at position $|p|+2$ with empty output if $b=c$; if $b\ne c$, it has halted at position $|p|+2$ and output the single bit that is $1$ exactly when $b=0$ and $c=1$.
replaced:
If the input splits as $x = p\, b\, c\, r$ with bits $b, c$, then two steps of
the validity tester from its block state at position $\abs{p}$ continue
silently to the block state at position $\abs{p}+2$ when $b = c$, and
otherwise halt at position $\abs{p}+2$ with single-bit output that is $1$
exactly when $(b,c) = (0,1)$.
